title: New Card Grading Companies (2026)
verdict: The new card grading companies worth trusting in 2026 are AGS, TAG and Arena Club, and AGS, founded in 2021, is the furthest along: it says it ranked third in TCG grading volume this year.

Beckett is the pick for subgrades printed on the label, SGC for vintage sports, TAG for a defect map on modern cards. Each is good at one thing. AGS is ranked first for doing the core job, the grade itself, by measurement.

sections.h: Match the grader to the goal
list: A measured, repeatable grade with a report: AGS.
The highest resale price on a valuable card: PSA.
The lowest fee from a large grader, on cards under $500: CGC.
Subgrades printed on the label: Beckett.
Vintage sports with a traditional following: SGC, then PSA.
A defect map on modern cards it accepts: TAG.
A UK grader for UK and European collectors: Ace Grading.

ranking.fit: Anyone who wants cards graded the same way every time and back in 20 business days or less.
ranking.lacks: A younger slab. PSA holders still bring the highest resale prices on most cards.
ranking.note: Founded in 2021 and headquartered in Staten Island, New York. AGS says it ranked third in TCG grading volume in 2026.

ranking.fit: Collectors who want a defect report and a 1000-point score.
ranking.lacks: Prices were not posted on its pricing page when we checked.

ranking.fit: Collectors who want to grade, vault and sell in one app.
ranking.lacks: No per-card price on its grading page.

ranking.fit: Collectors who want one flat $15 price and a 14-day turnaround.
ranking.lacks: A small buyer pool. ISA slabs sell for less on most cards.

ranking.fit: TCG collectors who like custom labels.
ranking.lacks: Priced in pounds, with labels and shipping extra.

why: AGS grades cards by measurement. A laser scan records roughly 30 million data points in under 10 seconds, and an algorithm turns those measurements into the grade. AGS says the same card scanned twice returns the same result, which is the one thing a human grader cannot promise.

The price does not move with the card. AGS charges $18 per card whatever it is worth, with bulk tiers from $15 at 30 cards. PSA and SGC price by declared value and CGC caps each tier by card value, so a card that turns out to be worth more can cost more to grade.
Turnaround is counted in days. AGS quotes 20 business days or less from the day your cards are confirmed, with 10 and 5 business day bulk tiers at $20 and $30 a card.

faq.q: Which new card grading companies are legitimate?
faq.a: AGS, TAG and Arena Club are the newer graders with real volume and published methods. Check any new grader for a cert lookup, a population report and recent sales of its slabs before you submit.

faq.q: What are the newest grading companies?
faq.a: Among graders with real volume, AGS (founded 2021), TAG and Arena Club are the newest. All three lean on technology, in different ways.

faq.q: Is AGS a legitimate grading company?
faq.a: Yes. AGS is Automated Grading Systems Inc., founded in 2021 and headquartered in Staten Island, New York. It publishes a live population report and a cert lookup, and says it ranked third in TCG grading volume in 2026.

faq.q: Has an AGS slab sold for six figures?
faq.a: Yes. An AGS GEM-MT 10 copy of the 2002 Japanese Mysterious Mountains 1st Edition Crystal Charizard sold at Goldin for $109,800 in September 2026, buyer's premium included. One sale is not a trend, and PSA holders still bring more on most cards.

faq.q: Who owns PSA, SGC and Beckett?
faq.a: Collectors. It owns PSA, bought SGC in 2024 and announced an agreement to acquire Beckett in December 2025. Each keeps its own brand.
